newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana yr/yr inflation falls to 42.6 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Ghana yr/yr inflation falls to 42.6 pct in July.

text.p: Ghana's year-on-year inflation rate fell to 42.6 percent in July, the seventh successive monthly fall, according to provisional figures released by the national statistics service.
The fall was in spite of a 1.3 percent increase on June, largely due to a rise in the cost of transport, communications, food, gross rent, fuel and power and clothing and footwear.
Inflation peaked at 70.8 percent in December but has been falling since then.
In June, the year-on-year rate was 48.4 percent. Year-on-year inflation in July 1995 was 67.2 percent.
The National Index in July (Base year 1977) stood at 69,511.8 compared with 48,731.2 in July 1995. It stood at 68,639.2 in June.

The government, which faces presidential and parliamentary elections in December, has an inflation target of 20 percent by the end of the year. It has been issuing high-rated Treasury bills and government bonds in a bid to reduce the money supply by soaking up excess liquidity in the economy. -- Abidjan newsroom +225 21 90 90
